summary: Calvin surveys the B system while Goku surveys A. Their reconnaissance finds wreckage from a destroyed USE vessel and then locates a Brazilian construction yard building new probes; the system's surveyed resources meet autofactory requirements. Calvin and Goku destroy the yard and its probes, although one vessel escapes; they claim the system, plan defensive replication with combat-class HEAVEN vessels, and decide to report to Bill and work in pairs more often.

introducing.name: Alpha Centauri B
introducing.description: The B star component of the Alpha Centauri system. It is more orange than Sol and has less than half Sol's luminosity; Calvin considers it less than ideal for a human home.

introducing.name: Alpha Centauri B 1
introducing.description: A small Mercury-like planet in an inner orbit around Alpha Centauri B.

introducing.name: asteroid belt
introducing.description: An asteroid belt identified during Calvin's survey of Alpha Centauri B. Scouts find wreckage there from a USE vessel, autofactory equipment, and fragments from two to three vessels.

introducing.name: asteroid belt
introducing.description: A second asteroid belt in Alpha Centauri B's comfort zone.

introducing.name: SURGE jammer
introducing.description: A jamming device used to interfere with an opponent's reactions during an attack.

updates.description: Small craft that investigate planets directly, filling a gap in the original mission design. In reconnaissance they activate at staggered distances on random vectors so an observer cannot trace the launching vessel, and modified SUDDAR arrays extend their survey range.

A subspace detection technology enabled by the same breakthrough as the SURGE drive. It can monitor distance, scan for threats and detect dense objects within a light-hour. An emitter flaw can give a much weaker ping with poor close-range sensitivity, which Bill suspects may reach farther. It gives little fine detail at long range, and a modified array can reach three light-hours at much lower resolution.
